newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank eases dollar sales limit.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank eases dollar sales limit.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board had decided to double the over-the-counter (OTC) dollar sales limit to $50,000 from $25,000, the Central Bank said on Thursday.
The new OTC limit is way below the $1 million-mark requested by the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP).
The BAP said the limit on the dollar sales of banks promote "underground" transactions.
But a Central Bank official said a very high ceiling for OTC dollar sales might encourage investors to circumvent current registration requirements.

The OTC transactions refer to non-trade dollar purchases from banks and foreign exchange dealers by walk-in clients that do not require documentation. These are used for travel, educational, advertising and royalty expenses, the Central Bank said.
This is one of the remaning steps for the further liberalisation of the country's foreign exchange market, the Central Bank said.
